ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a positively charged sulfur atom S; sulfur is connected to the R1 substituent on the left, the oxygen atom above, and the carbon atom on the right. The upper oxygen atom continues to connect to acetyl C(=O)CH3, forming an S-OAc connection. The right carbon atom is connected to H and R2. At the bottom of the figure, an independent AcO− acetate species is also drawn. There are also curved arrows in the figure, but the question requires ignoring the arrows. Reasoning: After ignoring the arrows, the sulfur center should be encoded as positively charged [S+]. R1 and R2 are generalized substituents, represented by the SMILES wildcard *; the carbon fragment where R2 is located can be written as *C[S+], and R1 on sulfur is written as [S+](*). Sulfur is also connected to acetyloxy, namely [S+]OC(C)=O, so the main fragment is *C[S+](*)OC(C)=O. The lower independent acetate AcO− is encoded as CC(=O)[O-]. The two disconnected components are connected with a dot, giving *C[S+](*)OC(C)=O.CC(=O)[O-].

raw_record.question_text: What is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image, ignoring the arrows?

method.method_draft: First visually transcribe the non-arrow bonds in the transition-state drawing. Convert the carbon–sulfur fragment with generic substituents into a wildcard-substituted skeleton, placing the positively charged sulfur as [S+] and attaching one wildcard substituent to sulfur and one wildcard-substituted carbon to sulfur. Then append the S–OAc connectivity as [S+]OC(C)=O. Finally encode the separate AcO− species as CC(=O)[O-] and join the two disconnected components with '.', yielding *C[S+](*)OC(C)=O.CC(=O)[O-].
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中有一个带正电的硫原子 S，硫连接到左侧的 R1 取代基、上方的氧原子以及右侧的碳原子。上方氧原子继续连接到乙酰基 C(=O)CH3，形成 S-OAc 连接。右侧碳原子连接 H 和 R2。图的下方还画有一个独立的 AcO− 乙酸根物种。图中还有弯箭头，但题目要求忽略箭头。
推理：忽略箭头后，硫中心应编码为带正电的 [S+]。R1 和 R2 是泛化取代基，用 SMILES 通配符 * 表示；其中 R2 所在的碳片段可写成 *C[S+]，硫上的 R1 写成 [S+](*)。硫还连接乙酰氧基，即 [S+]OC(C)=O，所以主片段为 *C[S+](*)OC(C)=O。下方独立的乙酸根 AcO− 编码为 CC(=O)[O-]。两个不连通组分用点号连接，得到 *C[S+](*)OC(C)=O.CC(=O)[O-]。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Direct structure-to-SMILES transcription is the natural single route for this problem; it is distinct because it relies on reading the drawn connectivity and charges rather than reaction-mechanism interpretation. With only one requested method, no weaker variants are needed.
planner_metadata.image_role: Inspect the drawing and ignore all curved arrows. Read the retained species: a central positively charged sulfur bonded to an R1 substituent, to the carbon bearing R2/H, and to an acetoxy oxygen; also a separate acetate anion labeled AcO−. Treat R1 and R2 as generic wildcard substituents.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text only to know the requested output format is a SMILES expression and that the curved arrows in the image must be ignored.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use SMILES conventions: generic R groups can be encoded as wildcard atoms '*'; charged sulfur is bracketed as [S+]; an acetoxy group attached through oxygen is OC(C)=O; a separate acetate anion is CC(=O)[O-]; disconnected species are separated by a dot.
